messages.subject: parallelReactives sketch idea
parts:
Hi,

  I have a shiny application to display data.  The data is loaded from a remote server (30s?) and then processed to fix date/time issues and decode json-like data in the rows (15 s).  Then it is run through ggplot (5s each plot).

  Each of these operations takes a long time, and blocks all users of the server.

  Ideally, the latency of these operations would not block the UI, but the UI would be updated when they are done.

  I have used curlMultiPerform to get data in the background, solving that block, but I still need to make the decoding, which is currently done in R, non blocking (asynchronous).

  I am going to start using parallel to fork radar tasks to do some of this work.  However, the code will have to be split into the parallelisable logic - that does NOT contain references to inputs or reactiveValues, and the marshaling logic which does the appropriate writes.

  In the longer run it would be great if this just worked in shiny.  I have investigated the options for 'threading' work in R, and the multicore library seems like a good bet.

  I'm thinking that shiny could just use parallel.  I'm thinking about the following scheme:

  parallelReactive({ ... })

  The parallelReactive body is spawned using the 'parallel' function.  

  parallel clones global state, so inputs would be visible.  The question is what to do with updated reactiveValues, and how to deal with plots.

  Plots should be simple enough if reactive values can be made to generate plots.  Note that currently plots are updated both on the input$ data (or reactive values) as well as the hidden inputs for width and height, and DPI

  It's not clear to me how to address plots, but I think you guys probably have a very solid idea.  Can you encapsulate the plot logic so it can be used to write to a reactiveValue instead of the output object?

  Dealing with reactiveValues requires a different solution.

  Parallel at the moment returns the final 'return' value from the child process to the parent, presumably serializing it and sending it across the pipe set-up by parallel from the child to the parent.

  For reactives to completely work the following would need to be true:

  * reads from inputs and reactiveValues need to be recorded and collected by the master
  * writes to reactiveValues need to be recorded (with values) and collected by the master
  * any final value required should also be collected, although since observe does not have a return value as such this seems less important - so unless outputs should also be parallelisable this isn't necessary
  * the parallelized jobs should be monitored asynchronously and when the job finished, all of the above should be combined, and the global reactiveValues and reactive control tables in the master should be updated based upon what happened in the child.
  * any discrepancy between the state used by the reactive and the state when the job has finished before collection should betaken account of to see if the reactive computed a value which isn't needed any more

  Since the master is able to keep track of such reads and changes to inputs and reactiveValues, the child should in theory have this capability too.

  So: 
  When a parallel child starts, create an empty log
  So: when a reactiveValue is updated AND we are executing in a parallel child context, update the log with the name of the reactive, the action performed, and the associated values
  When the parallel child is about to return, marshal all these into a single data structure
  When the job finishes, master process shiny polls or otherwise detects the job has finished, and invokes a cleanup handler in the master which performs the above steps.

  It feels to me like shiny already needs to perform most of these things, so it would be a matter of fitting awareness of parallel state into shiny, and handling the cleanup logic.

----

  Joe, Winston, what are your feel ins on this matter?

-Alex
